stories.headline: Samsung guides record $80B Q3 operating profit on AI memory; TSMC books record quarter

key_facts.fact: Samsung Electronics estimated third-quarter (July-September) operating profit at 107.4 trillion won (about $80.2 billion), up 782.5% year on year, in a preliminary filing on October 8 KST.
key_facts.excerpt: Samsung Electronics estimated its operating profit for the July-September period at 107.4 trillion won ($80.2 billion), topping 100 trillion won for a quarter for the first time on continued memory demand. The figure jumped 782.5 percent from a year earlier

key_facts.fact: Preliminary Q3 revenue was 195 trillion won, up about 127% year on year, implying an operating margin of roughly 55%.
key_facts.excerpt: Sales are estimated at 195 trillion won, or $145.6 billion (€129.9bn), up 127% year-on-year, implying an operating margin of about 55%.

key_facts.fact: It is the first time a South Korean company topped 100 trillion won in quarterly operating profit, Samsung's fourth straight record quarter, and above Nvidia's $63.7 billion operating income in its latest quarter.
key_facts.excerpt: beating the $63.7 billion (€56.8bn) in operating income that US chip designer Nvidia booked in its latest quarter. It would also be the first time a South Korean company's quarterly operating profit had topped 100 trillion won (€66.6bn), and Samsung's fourth record quarter in a row.

key_facts.fact: The profit slightly beat the LSEG SmartEstimate of 106.1 trillion won; growth was driven by memory demand from AI data centers, including HBM.
key_facts.excerpt: The world's largest memory chipmaker estimated an operating profit of 107.4 trillion won ($80.17 billion) for the July-September period, slightly ahead of an LSEG SmartEstimate of 106.1 trillion won.

key_facts.fact: Samsung shares closed 2.42% lower at 262,000 won on Thursday as investors took profits; the KOSPI fell 2.62%. Full results are due October 29.
key_facts.excerpt: Its shares nonetheless closed 2.42% lower at 262,000 won in Seoul on Thursday, as investors took profits and questioned how long the memory boom can last, while the benchmark KOSPI index lost 2.62%.

key_facts.fact: Analysts estimate Samsung's foundry and System LSI business still lost around 1 trillion to 1.5 trillion won, partly due to start-up costs at the Taylor, Texas fab.
key_facts.excerpt: the non-memory business, comprising System LSI and foundry operations, is estimated to have continued to post a loss of around KRW 1 trillion to KRW 1.5 trillion, due to initial costs associated with the startup of the Taylor fab in Texas.

key_facts.fact: TSMC said on October 8 that September revenue rose 54.6% to NT$511.86 billion, taking Q3 revenue to a record NT$1.49 trillion (about $46.8 billion), above the top of its $44.6-45.8 billion guidance.
key_facts.excerpt: said on Thursday that September revenue rose 54.6% year-on-year to NT$511.86 billion... took estimated third-quarter revenue, calculated from its monthly figures, to a record NT$1.49 trillion, or $46.8 billion (€41.8bn), up 51% on a year earlier... The total beat the top of TSMC's own guidance of $44.6 billion (€39.8bn) to $45.8 billion

stories.headline: GlobalFoundries signs $2B, five-year deal to make CoWoS silicon interposers for TSMC in New York

key_facts.fact: GlobalFoundries announced on October 8 a manufacturing agreement with TSMC to establish a U.S.-based supply of silicon interposers for TSMC's CoWoS advanced packaging ecosystem.
key_facts.excerpt: GlobalFoundries (Nasdaq: GFS) (GF) today announced a manufacturing agreement with TSMC to establish a U.S.-based supply of silicon interposers for TSMC's CoWoS ® advanced packaging ecosystem.

key_facts.fact: The multi-year agreement is worth $2 billion and has an initial term of five years.
key_facts.excerpt: Multi-year $2 billion agreement will expand capacity for advanced packaging ecosystem... The agreement has an initial term of five years and provides a framework for future capacity expansion.

key_facts.fact: GF will add capacity at its Malta, New York fab, which is expected to become the first U.S. source of silicon interposers; volume production is expected to ramp in the first half of 2028.
key_facts.excerpt: The Malta facility is expected to become the first US-based source of silicon interposers used in advanced chip-packaging technologies... volume production expected to begin ramping up in the first half of 2028

key_facts.fact: A silicon interposer sits beneath processors and memory chips inside advanced AI packages and lets them communicate at high speed.
key_facts.excerpt: Known as a silicon interposer, the component sits beneath processors and memory chips inside advanced AI packages and enables them to communicate at high speeds.

key_facts.fact: The interposers include embedded deep trench capacitor components, according to GF.
key_facts.excerpt: establish the first U.S.-based source of silicon interposers supporting advanced packaging technologies, including embedded deep trench capacitor components.

key_facts.fact: Coverage of the deal describes GlobalFoundries as UAE-backed.
key_facts.excerpt: UAE-backed semiconductor manufacturer GlobalFoundries has announced a $2 billion deal with Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company to bolster US chip manufacturing.

stories.headline: Broadcom seeks $50B+ in private credit to fund OpenAI's custom chips; Oracle in chip-lease talks

key_facts.fact: Broadcom is working to arrange more than $50 billion in financing for the custom AI chip it is building with OpenAI, with Apollo and Blackstone among lenders approached, the Wall Street Journal reported on October 7.
key_facts.excerpt: Broadcom is working to arrange more than $50 billion in financing for OpenAI's custom AI chip, with Apollo and Blackstone among the lenders approached, according to the Wall Street Journal

key_facts.fact: Talks are early and the size could change; the deal is expected to close before year-end and could cover several gigawatts of OpenAI chip capacity.
key_facts.excerpt: The proposed financing could support several gigawatts of chip capacity for OpenAI... with Broadcom and OpenAI expecting the deal to close by year-end. Discussions remain preliminary, and the final amount could change

key_facts.fact: OpenAI's chip program is internally called Nexus, with first- and second-generation parts codenamed Jalapeño and Serrano.
key_facts.excerpt: According to the WSJ, OpenAI's internal chip initiative, known as Nexus, includes custom processors named after peppers. Its first two generations are Jalapeño and Serrano.

key_facts.fact: Bloomberg reported a smaller figure of around $30 billion in debt for the next phase of the project, saying no formal process has begun.
key_facts.excerpt: Bloomberg reports that discussions point to around $30 billion in debt for the next phase of the project, while The Wall Street Journal says Broadcom has been working to arrange more than $50 billion

key_facts.fact: Oracle is in talks with Apollo and Goldman Sachs on a framework to buy hardware for a 1-gigawatt data center, under which private investors would fund an off-balance-sheet entity that buys chips and leases them to Oracle.
key_facts.excerpt: Oracle is negotiating with Apollo and Goldman Sachs on a dedicated financing framework aimed at procuring hardware for a 1-gigawatt data center facility. Under the proposed structure, private investors would fund an off-balance-sheet entity to buy the chips and lease them back to Oracle

key_facts.fact: Separately, a $60 billion chip financing package partly backed by Broadcom, with Anthropic among the main beneficiaries, includes $42 billion of senior-secured debt and $18 billion of junior debt led by Blackstone.
key_facts.excerpt: A separate $60 billion AI chip financing package backed in part by Broadcom is also moving forward, with Anthropic among the main beneficiaries. The package includes $42 billion in senior-secured debt backed by residual-value support from Broadcom and $18 billion in junior debt led by Blackstone

stories.headline: Nvidia-backed Firmus's A$44B ASX float falters as bankers weigh repricing or pulling the IPO

key_facts.fact: Firmus's institutional bookbuild closed on Thursday October 8 (9am Australian time) after investors balked at the A$11-a-share price, which implied a valuation of about A$43.7 billion (US$30.3 billion).
key_facts.excerpt: Institutional investors were due to submit their bids for shares, initially priced at $11, by Thursday at 9am... the company had still priced the IPO at $11 a share, implying a valuation of about $43.7 billion ($30.3 billion).

key_facts.fact: Bankers moved from discussing a reworked float with a lower market cap to considering pulling the deal altogether, the Australian Financial Review reported.
key_facts.excerpt: In a dramatic turn early on Thursday, bankers working on the proposed $44 billion listing veered from discussing the need to rework the float, cutting the company's market capitalisation, to considering pulling the deal altogether.

key_facts.fact: Firmus and its advisers were contemplating cutting the offer price from A$11 to A$8.25; shares of Maas Group, which owns 3.2% of Firmus, plunged 30%.
key_facts.excerpt: Investor concerns that Nvidia-backed Firmus may cut the size of its $5 billion Australian initial public offering (IPO) drove a 30% plunge in shares of construction services provider Maas Group, which owns 3.2% in the AI data centre operator... reducing the price per share from A$11 each to A$8.25

key_facts.fact: Firmus was seeking to raise about A$7 billion (roughly US$5 billion) in what would be Australia's second-largest IPO after Telstra; it is scheduled to list on the ASX on October 23.
key_facts.excerpt: It was touted as the biggest float since Telstra in the 1990s... Reports suggest Firmus intends to raise up to $7 billion from institutional and retail investors... The company is scheduled to float on the ASX on October 23.

key_facts.fact: Firmus runs 46MW of capacity today with 865MW across five projects under way, contracted to Meta, OpenAI and Fireworks AI; Nvidia holds 7.2% and Blackstone 6.7%.
key_facts.excerpt: It has 46MW running and 865MW in five projects under way in Indonesia, Malaysia and Tasmania, contracted to Meta, OpenAI and Fireworks AI. ... existing backers, including Nvidia (7.2%) and Blackstone (6.7%).

key_facts.fact: Once its data centres are built, Firmus expects to carry about US$30 billion of debt, around six times the US$5 billion of operating earnings it forecasts for 2028.
key_facts.excerpt: Once its data centres are built, Firmus expects to be carrying about US$30 billion of debt, around six times the US$5 billion of operating earnings it forecasts for 2028.

stories.headline: Nvidia opens RTX Spark Arm PC chip preorders with Microsoft's $2,599 Surface Laptop Ultra

key_facts.fact: At a Microsoft event in San Francisco on October 7, Jensen Huang and Satya Nadella outlined jointly engineered hardware and software for AI agents on Windows PCs; RTX Spark laptop preorders opened that day, with availability from October 16 and compact desktops in November.
key_facts.excerpt: RTX Spark puts the full NVIDIA AI stack into Windows laptops and compact desktops, with laptop preorders open today and available October 16. Compact desktops will be available for sale in November.

key_facts.fact: RTX Spark combines a Blackwell RTX GPU with up to 6,144 cores and an up to 20-core Grace CPU linked at 600 GB/s, delivering one petaflop of FP4 AI performance with up to 128GB of unified memory.
key_facts.excerpt: The hardware combines an NVIDIA Blackwell RTX GPU with up to 6,144 cores and an up to 20-core NVIDIA Grace CPU connected at 600 GB/s. It offers one petaflop of FP4 AI performance and up to 128GB of unified memory.

key_facts.fact: Microsoft's Surface Laptop Ultra, powered by RTX Spark, starts at $2,599 and reaches $5,899; a Surface RTX Spark Dev Box costs $5,999.
key_facts.excerpt: the new Surface Laptop Ultra, priced at $2,599 for the base configuration... reaching up to $5,899 for the top-end configuration... Surface RTX Spark Dev Box, which features 128 GB of RAM, 2 TB of storage, 20 CPU cores, and 6,144 GPU cores for $5,999.

key_facts.fact: The new machines run Windows 11 on Nvidia's Arm-based N1X chip family, co-designed with MediaTek, making them Windows-on-Arm devices.
key_facts.excerpt: the new small desktops, Surface Dev Box, and laptops run Windows 11 on Nvidia's N1X family of chips... these chips are based on the Arm CPU architecture, with MediaTek contributing to their design, meaning these are Windows on Arm devices.

key_facts.fact: Systems are coming from Acer, ASUS, Dell, HP, Lenovo, Microsoft, MSI and Gigabyte.
key_facts.excerpt: Systems are coming from Acer, ASUS, Dell, HP, Lenovo, Microsoft, MSI and Gigabyte, Nvidia says.

key_facts.fact: Nvidia also previewed DGX Station for Windows on the GB300 Grace Blackwell Ultra Desktop Superchip, with 748GB of coherent memory and up to 20 petaflops of FP4 compute.
key_facts.excerpt: NVIDIA DGX Station for Windows runs on the GB300 Grace Blackwell Ultra Desktop Superchip, delivering 748GB of coherent memory and up to 20 petaFLOPS of FP4 AI compute

stories.headline: Quantum hardware startup Oratomic raises $475M at $5.4B; Universal Quantum raises $100M+

key_facts.fact: Oratomic raised a $475 million Series B co-led by ARCH Venture Partners, Spark Capital, Khosla Ventures, Index Ventures, General Catalyst and Bezos Expeditions, three months after its Series A.
key_facts.excerpt: Quantum computing startup Oratomic raised $475 million, just three months after its Series A... ARCH Venture Partners, Spark Capital, Khosla Ventures, Index Ventures, General Catalyst and Bezos Expeditions co-led the Series-B round

key_facts.fact: The round brings Oratomic's total funding to $775 million and lifts its valuation to $5.4 billion from $1.5 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: bringing the company's total funding raised to date to $775 million, and bumping its valuation to $5.4 billion from $1.5 billion.

key_facts.fact: Pasadena-based Oratomic, founded in 2025 and led by CEO Dolev Bluvstein, expects to have a large-scale, fault-tolerant quantum computer ready by 2030.
key_facts.excerpt: CEO and co-founder Dolev Bluvstein said the company will use the capital to tackle engineering challenges as it develops a large-scale, fault-tolerant quantum computer that it expects to have ready by 2030.

key_facts.fact: Oratomic uses reconfigurable neutral-atom arrays and believes it can build a useful fault-tolerant machine with only about 10,000 qubits.
key_facts.excerpt: California-based Oratomic, which uses reconfigurable neutral-atom arrays, raised $475 million... Oratomic believes it can build a quantum computer with only 10,000 qubits and still maintain high

key_facts.fact: UK-based Universal Quantum, which develops modular trapped-ion systems, raised more than $100 million in Series A funding the same day.
key_facts.excerpt: United Kingdom-based Universal Quantum Ltd., which develops modular trapped-ion systems, raised more than $100 million in Series A funding.

stories.headline: Robot-data startup Mecka AI raises $60M Series B led by Sequoia, with Nvidia and Samsung

key_facts.fact: Mecka announced on October 7 a $60 million Series B led by Sequoia Capital, with new investors Nvidia, Microsoft's M12, Qualcomm Ventures and Samsung.
key_facts.excerpt: Today, we're announcing that Mecka has raised a $60 million Series B led by Sequoia Capital, backed by new investors including NVIDIA, M12 — Microsoft's Venture Fund, Qualcomm Ventures and Samsung

key_facts.fact: Angels include DoorDash CEO Tony Xu, former ServiceNow and Snowflake CEO Frank Slootman, and Milan Kovac, former head of Tesla's Optimus program.
key_facts.excerpt: Tony Xu, founder and CEO of DoorDash; Frank Slootman, former CEO of ServiceNow and Snowflake; Milan Kovac, former head of Optimus at Tesla and many more.

key_facts.fact: Mecka pays people to record themselves doing everyday tasks while wearing body sensors and using smartphones, to train humanoid and other robots; TechCrunch had earlier reported the round at a valuation of about $500 million.
key_facts.excerpt: Mecka pays people to record themselves doing everyday tasks, like making coffee or fixing cars, while wearing body sensors and using smartphones... TechCrunch had previously reported that the startup was nearing a new funding round at a $500 million valuation.

key_facts.fact: The New York- and Toronto-based startup has disclosed $128 million in funding, says it passed $100 million in annual run-rate revenue by June 2026, and expects $300 million by year-end.
key_facts.excerpt: The New York and Toronto startup has now disclosed $128 million across three ... million as of ... 26 and expects ... reach $300 million by year end.

key_facts.fact: Mecka says the capital will scale its data infrastructure, deepen its research lab and build out commercial robot deployment, positioning itself as a robotics integrator that brings hardware, data capture and post-training.
key_facts.excerpt: The capital scales our data infrastructure, deepens our internal research lab, and builds out commercial robot deployment — the data and deployment layer for robotics... We bring the hardware, data capture, post-training, integration, and ongoing operations.
